# Nagi Mesa / Softpipe patch boundary

The Mesa source at `third_party/mesa/` is generated by `nagi fetch` from the
exact revision in `third_party/sources.lock`. It is not vendored into the Nagi
repository. Nagi-specific Mesa changes must be represented here as numbered
patches and applied only after `git apply --check` succeeds.

The M17 software-rendering design uses Mesa's Gallium `softpipe` driver. The
source lock records the dereferenced Mesa 24.3.0 revision
`f1f246cfda65eff82fba3be1caf2d23bdeda60cc`; the annotated tag object is not
used as a build identity. Mesa has component-specific notices, so a build
must preserve the upstream notice files and review the licenses of each
enabled component.

`0001-nagi-platform-static-softpipe.patch` is the Nagi-specific source
boundary. It adds the `nagi` Meson platform, permits EGL without a host DRI
device, links EGL to the built-in Gallium `softpipe` archive, and makes the
Nagi EGL and glapi libraries static archives while retaining Mesa's required
glapi feature. It also avoids probing target-only `ETIME`
and accepts LLVM's `llvm-nm` tool name. The patch is intentionally small: it
does not add a host display backend or make a host GL context available.

`0002-nagi-os-time.patch` extends Mesa's OS detection for the explicit
`__NAGI__` cross-build define and routes Mesa's monotonic clock/sleep helpers
through the Nagi POSIX clock ABI. It does not use host time or a host sleep
implementation.

`0003-nagi-static-loader.patch` makes Mesa's optional dynamic-loader helper
explicitly unavailable on Nagi. M17 links EGL and Softpipe statically, so this
prevents `dlopen`/`dlsym`/`dlclose` from becoming accidental unresolved guest
dependencies; it does not fabricate a symbol lookup result or load a host
library.

`0004-nagi-os-misc.patch` supplies the Nagi `unistd.h` include for Mesa's
POSIX-lite system-information helper and makes the unavailable physical-page
query fail truthfully instead of treating Nagi as an unknown platform. The
page-size path remains backed by Nagi `sysconf`.

`0005-nagi-qsort-freestanding.patch` removes Mesa's unused `<thread>` header
from `u_qsort.cpp`. The implementation uses the C++ `thread_local` language
storage specifier directly; the standard header is not needed and cannot be
resolved for the freestanding Nagi target without introducing a host C++
runtime.

`0006-nagi-disable-astc-cpp-transcode.patch` keeps Nagi's first software-
rendering slice on Mesa's existing CPU ASTC fallback path. It excludes the
optional Granite ASTC LUT/GPU-transcode utility, whose C++ standard-library
containers and mutexes are not part of the freestanding target runtime, and
returns failure from the optional transcode hook so the caller uses its
existing fallback. It does not claim ASTC GPU transcoding support.

`0007-nagi-static-loader-null.patch` supplies the standard `stddef.h` include
needed by Mesa's statically disabled loader fallback, where upstream normally
gets `NULL` from a host loader header. It adds no loader behavior or host
library dependency.

`0008-nagi-debug-strings-header.patch` makes Mesa's `u_debug.c` include the
POSIX `strings.h` declaration for `strcasecmp`. The pinned relibc target
already provides the real function; this patch removes an accidental reliance
on transitive host libc headers.

`0009-nagi-drm-uapi-ioctl-header.patch` gives Mesa's DRM UAPI header an
explicit Nagi branch using relibc's real `sys/ioctl.h` ABI instead of the BSD
`sys/ioccom.h` header. It preserves the UAPI integer layout and does not add a
host DRM device or host ioctl path.

`0010-nagi-alloca-header.patch` makes Mesa's C99 alloca helper include the
existing relibc `alloca.h` when compiling for Nagi. The target header exposes
the compiler builtin macro; this removes an accidental dependency on a host
libc's transitive `stdlib.h` declaration without adding a runtime allocator.

`0011-nagi-strings-header.patch` makes Mesa's common string helper include
relibc's POSIX `strings.h` for Nagi. This supplies the real `strcasecmp`
declaration to all compiled users of that helper instead of relying on a host
libc's transitive declarations.

`0012-nagi-glsl-dynarray.patch` replaces the selected GLSL precision pass's
`std::vector` containers with Mesa's real `util_dynarray`, avoiding a host C++
STL dependency while retaining target allocator-backed storage.

`0013-nagi-astc-cstdlib.patch` selects relibc's real C `stdlib.h` for the
Nagi ASTC CPU decoder's `abort()` calls; other platforms retain Mesa's
`<cstdlib>` include.

`0014-nagi-disable-hud-signals.patch` excludes only Mesa HUD's optional
signal-toggle handler on Nagi because the first-pixel path does not use it and
Nagi's signal ABI is not a compile-time substitute for an implemented signal
delivery path. HUD drawing and Softpipe remain enabled.

`0015-nagi-egl-native-types.patch` adds the Nagi EGL native handle types used
by the existing Surfman Nagi surfaceless FFI (`void *` for display, pixmap,
and window); it does not introduce a host window-system backend.

`0016-nagi-static-egl-without-dri.patch` records the first build-graph
separation experiment: it removes Nagi from Mesa's broad `with_dri` condition
so the unused shared DRI target is not generated. The next patch refines that
boundary after Mesa's EGL configuration check showed that the DRI frontend is
also the real surfaceless EGL implementation.

`0017-nagi-static-egl-dri-frontend.patch` keeps Mesa's DRI2 frontend and
`libdri` static archive for Nagi's surfaceless EGL path, while gating only the
shared `src/gallium/targets/dri` `libgallium` target on non-Nagi platforms.
EGL therefore links the static frontend, pipe loader, and real Softpipe driver;
no dynamic DRI module or host device is introduced.

`0018-nagi-enable-dri2-frontend.patch` enables the DRI2 frontend source for
the Nagi surfaceless build. Mesa's drawable dispatch references the real
`dri2_init_drawable` implementation for its configured screen types; this
patch includes that implementation in `libdri` without enabling a host DRM
platform or dynamic driver.

`0019-nagi-vtn-generated-header.patch` propagates Mesa's generated SPIR-V
metadata header through the real `idep_vtn` dependency. The explicitly built
`libmesa.a` target contains `glspirv.c`, so the generated header must be a
declared target source even though the normal default target graph may reach it
through another archive. This changes only Meson's dependency graph; it does
not replace SPIR-V compilation or add a host header.

The intended guest build is a static, cross-compiled Meson build with
`-Dgallium-drivers=softpipe`, `-Dplatforms=nagi`,
`-Degl-native-platform=surfaceless`, LLVM disabled, and zlib/zstd/shader-cache
disabled. The Nagi cross file uses `x86_64-unknown-elf` only as the Clang
freestanding code-generation triple; the Meson host system remains `nagi`.
The build consumes C headers generated from the pinned Nagi relibc checkout.
Those headers are an ABI prerequisite, not a host sysroot substitute.

The adjacent `tools/mesa/nagi-headers/new` header is Nagi-owned C++ language
support for the freestanding Mesa compile. It provides placement-new syntax and
declares the ordinary allocation operators; their definitions must be supplied
by the Nagi user allocator at final link and are not provided by a host C++
runtime.

`egl-native-platform=surfaceless` is a build setting, not permission to use a
host display. The Nagi adapter owns the framebuffer allocation and readback;
no host GL context or screenshot bridge is permitted.
